figures.title: This paper in the 13 components, against the field
figures.subtitle: Each box: what this paper does, then common practice across all sensors and how many ledger papers share it.
figures.caption: Verdicts compare the paper's choice for each component with common practice across 8,995 ledger entries on any sensor (silent speech, brain-to-text, lip reading), not only lip-reading papers.

M01.note: Inherited from the LRW pipeline; broadcast voiced speech is the field default.

M02.note: Automatic subtitle-aligned labels inherited from LRW; standard for broadcast data.

M03.note: First length curriculum in the wiki and widely copied, but the 76.5 to 61.1% WER gain is one run and was later attributed to sub-sequence augmentation, so not ahead.

M04.note: Inherited; voiced speech at use time is the field default.

M05.note: Inherited from LRW; camera mouth ROI plus microphone is the field default.

M06.field: Attention seq2seq decoding from non-audio signals
M06.note: LAS imported from audio ASR; no decoder comparison on LRS and LRW/GRID results are fine-tunes of the LRS model, so method and data scale are confounded and it is not ahead.

M07.note: No external LM with beam 4 is ordinary practice for attention decoders.

M09.note: Offline benchmark study; confirmation does not apply.

M10.note: Offline benchmark study; correction does not apply.

M11.field: In-the-wild sentence test sets; speaker-disjoint only in some
M11.note: LRS made in-the-wild sentence lipreading measurable, but train/test speaker overlap is not reported and BBC presenters recur across broadcasts.

choice: CER, WER, unigram BLEU; one run
M12.field: Machine vs human lipreader on the same material
M12.note: The machine beats the lipreader in direction, but whether 50.2% was scored on the same 200 clips and run-to-run variance are not reported.

choice: Release promised in arXiv v2 only; never released
M13.note: Compute is reported; the dataset release promised in arXiv v2 was dropped from the CVF version and LRS stayed unreleased.
